name: Pharma GMP Pack
description: GMP self-inspection content for finished pharmaceuticals: quality unit, training, equipment, deviations and CAPA, batch record review, data integrity (ALCOA+), QC laboratory, change control, supplier qualification, complaints and self-inspection. Mapped to 21 CFR 210/211 and Part 11, EU GMP and Annex 11, PIC/S PE 009, ICH Q10 and Schedule M.
disclaimer: Clause summaries are paraphrased for retrieval and citation only; they are not the authoritative regulatory text. Schedule M section numbering is pending confirmation. All entries are draft pending review by a pharma QA domain expert.

clauses.title: Responsibilities of quality control unit
clauses.summary: A quality control unit with authority to approve or reject components, products, procedures and records, and to review production records, must exist with written responsibilities.

clauses.title: Personnel qualifications
clauses.summary: Personnel must have the education, training and experience to perform their functions, including cGMP training conducted by qualified individuals with sufficient frequency.

clauses.title: Equipment cleaning and maintenance
clauses.summary: Equipment must be cleaned, maintained and sanitised at appropriate intervals under written procedures, with records of cleaning and maintenance.

clauses.title: Automatic, mechanical and electronic equipment
clauses.summary: Computerised equipment must be routinely calibrated, inspected or checked; controls must ensure only authorised personnel make changes to master records, and backups must be maintained.

clauses.title: Testing and approval or rejection of components
clauses.summary: Each lot of components must be sampled, tested or examined and approved before use; reliance on supplier certificates of analysis requires supplier qualification and periodic verification.

clauses.title: Written procedures; deviations
clauses.summary: Written production and process control procedures must be followed and documented; any deviation must be recorded and justified.

clauses.title: Batch production and control records
clauses.summary: Batch records must include complete information on production and control of each batch, including dates, equipment, materials, in-process results, signatures of persons performing and checking each step.

clauses.title: Production record review
clauses.summary: Production and control records must be reviewed and approved by the quality unit before release; unexplained discrepancies or failures must be thoroughly investigated and extended to other batches that may be affected, with written conclusions and follow-up.

clauses.title: Laboratory records
clauses.summary: Laboratory records must include complete data from all tests, including raw data, calculations, signatures of the analyst and reviewer.

clauses.title: Complaint files
clauses.summary: Written procedures for handling complaints must exist; complaints are reviewed by the quality unit and investigated where appropriate, with records maintained.

clauses.title: Limiting system access
clauses.summary: System access must be limited to authorised individuals.

clauses.title: Audit trails
clauses.summary: Secure, computer-generated, time-stamped audit trails must independently record the date and time of operator entries and actions that create, modify or delete electronic records; changes must not obscure previous values.

clauses.title: Controls for identification codes/passwords
clauses.summary: Identification code and password combinations must be unique, periodically checked, and withdrawn when compromised.

clauses.title: Validation
clauses.summary: Computerised systems must be validated over their life cycle, with documented user requirements and evidence that the system performs as intended.

clauses.title: Audit trails
clauses.summary: Based on risk, systems should record GMP-relevant changes and deletions with reason; audit trails must be available and regularly reviewed.

clauses.title: Change and configuration management
clauses.summary: Changes to a computerised system, including configuration, should be made only in a controlled manner under a defined procedure.

clauses.title: Security
clauses.summary: Physical and logical controls should restrict access to computerised systems to authorised persons; creation, change and cancellation of access authorisations should be recorded.

clauses.title: Complaints, quality defects and product recalls
clauses.summary: Complaints and potential quality defects are recorded and investigated with appropriate root cause analysis and CAPA, and recall capability is maintained.

clauses.title: Self inspection
clauses.summary: Self inspections are conducted to monitor implementation and compliance with GMP and to propose corrective measures; they are recorded and followed up.

clauses.title: Self inspection
clauses.summary: Equivalent to EU GMP Chapter 9: planned, independent and recorded self inspections with follow-up of corrective actions.

clauses.title: Corrective action and preventive action (CAPA) system
clauses.summary: CAPA should result from investigation of complaints, deviations, non-conformances, audits and trends; the effectiveness of CAPA should be evaluated.

clauses.title: Change management system
clauses.summary: Proposed changes should be evaluated, using quality risk management, approved and their implementation evaluated after the change.

clauses.title: Pharmaceutical quality system
clauses.summary: Manufacturers must establish a pharmaceutical quality system covering quality risk management, product quality review, deviation, CAPA and change control. Section numbering to be confirmed by domain expert.

clauses.title: Self-inspection, quality audits and supplier audits
clauses.summary: Regular self-inspections and quality audits must be performed and recorded, including audits and approval of suppliers. Section numbering to be confirmed by domain expert.

clauses.title: Documentation and records
clauses.summary: Documents and records must be designed, prepared, reviewed and controlled so that the history of each batch is traceable. Section numbering to be confirmed by domain expert.

controls.title: Quality unit authority and responsibilities are defined and exercised
controls.objective: The quality unit independently approves or rejects materials, procedures and batches.
controls.risk: Product released without independent quality oversight.
testOfDesign: Inspect the quality manual and organisation chart for QU independence and written responsibilities.
testOfEffectiveness: Confirm sampled batch releases, SOP approvals and specification changes were approved by the QU.
checklist: Is the QU independent of production?
Are QU responsibilities written and current?
controls.recommendation: Document QU responsibilities and ensure all releases and GMP document approvals carry QU sign-off.

controls.title: GMP training is current for all personnel
controls.objective: Staff are trained on cGMP and on the SOPs for their role before performing tasks.
controls.risk: Errors from untrained staff performing GMP activities.
testOfDesign: Inspect the training procedure, role-based curricula and qualification of trainers.
testOfEffectiveness: For sampled staff who performed batch steps confirm training on the relevant SOP version was completed before the task date.
checklist: Was training complete before task performance?
Is annual GMP refresher training current?
controls.recommendation: Link role curricula to SOP versions and block task assignment until training is complete.

controls.title: Equipment cleaning and maintenance are performed and logged
controls.objective: Equipment is cleaned and maintained per schedule with contemporaneous logbook entries.
controls.risk: Cross-contamination or equipment failure affecting product quality.
testOfDesign: Inspect cleaning SOPs, cleaning validation and preventive maintenance schedule.
testOfEffectiveness: For sampled equipment and batches confirm logbook entries for cleaning and maintenance are complete and timely.
checklist: Are logbook entries contemporaneous and signed?
Is preventive maintenance on schedule?
controls.recommendation: Enforce contemporaneous logbook entries and track preventive maintenance overdue items.

controls.title: Deviations are recorded, investigated and extended to other batches
controls.objective: Every deviation is documented, root-caused and assessed for impact on other batches.
controls.risk: Recurring failures and affected batches released.
testOfDesign: Inspect the deviation procedure for classification, timelines, root cause tools and batch impact assessment.
testOfEffectiveness: For sampled deviations confirm timely closure, documented root cause, and impact extended to other potentially affected batches.
checklist: Were investigations closed within the SOP timeline?
Was impact on other batches assessed?
Is root cause supported by evidence?
controls.recommendation: Strengthen root cause analysis and require documented batch impact assessment for every deviation.

controls.title: CAPA effectiveness is verified
controls.objective: Corrective and preventive actions are implemented and verified as effective.
controls.risk: Ineffective CAPA leading to repeat observations and 483s.
testOfDesign: Inspect the CAPA procedure for effectiveness-check criteria and timing.
testOfEffectiveness: For sampled closed CAPAs confirm effectiveness checks were performed against defined criteria; check for recurrence.
checklist: Are effectiveness criteria defined up front?
Has the issue recurred after closure?
controls.recommendation: Define measurable effectiveness criteria for every CAPA and verify them before closure.

controls.title: Batch records are complete and reviewed by QA before release
controls.objective: Every batch record is complete, reviewed and approved by QA before release.
controls.risk: Release of batches with undetected errors or missing data.
testOfDesign: Inspect the batch record review SOP and release checklist.
testOfEffectiveness: For sampled released batches confirm the batch record is complete, all entries signed and checked, and QA review completed before release.
checklist: Are all critical steps signed by performer and checker?
Was QA review completed before release?
controls.recommendation: Use a release checklist that blocks release until batch record review is complete and discrepancies are resolved.

controls.title: Audit trails are enabled and reviewed
controls.objective: GMP-relevant changes in computerised systems are captured in audit trails that are reviewed.
testOfDesign: Confirm audit trails are enabled and cannot be disabled by users on HPLC/LIMS/MES; inspect the audit trail review SOP.
testOfEffectiveness: For sampled analyses or batches confirm audit trail review was performed and documented before result approval.
checklist: Are audit trails enabled on all GMP systems?
Is audit trail review performed before release?
controls.recommendation: Enable audit trails on all GMP systems and make audit trail review a documented step before result approval.

controls.title: Unique user accounts and controlled access to GMP systems
controls.objective: Each user has a unique account with role-appropriate access; no shared or generic accounts.
controls.risk: Actions cannot be attributed to individuals, undermining data integrity.
testOfDesign: Inspect user management SOP and role definitions for GMP systems.
testOfEffectiveness: Obtain user lists for sampled systems; confirm no shared accounts, leavers removed, and admin rights segregated from users.
checklist: Are there shared or generic accounts?
Do analysts have admin rights?
controls.recommendation: Remove shared accounts, segregate administrator rights and review access quarterly.

controls.title: Laboratory records are complete and OOS results investigated
controls.objective: Laboratory data are complete and out-of-specification results are investigated.
controls.risk: Invalid results or testing into compliance.
testOfDesign: Inspect the OOS procedure and laboratory documentation practices.
testOfEffectiveness: For sampled tests confirm complete raw data, analyst and reviewer signatures; for sampled OOS confirm phase I/II investigations were completed and justified.
checklist: Is raw data complete?
Were OOS results invalidated only with a scientifically justified root cause?
controls.recommendation: Require scientifically justified root cause before invalidating any OOS result and trend OOS by product and test.

controls.title: Changes are controlled through risk-based change control
controls.objective: GMP-relevant changes are assessed, approved and verified before and after implementation.
controls.risk: Unassessed changes affecting validated state or product quality.
testOfDesign: Inspect the change control SOP for risk assessment, approvals and post-implementation review.
testOfEffectiveness: For sampled changes confirm QA approval before implementation and post-implementation effectiveness review.
checklist: Was QA approval obtained before implementation?
Was post-implementation review completed?
controls.recommendation: Ensure every GMP change has QA pre-approval and a post-implementation review.

controls.title: Suppliers of components are qualified and monitored
controls.objective: Components come from qualified suppliers; reliance on COAs is supported by verification testing.
controls.risk: Substandard or adulterated components entering production.
testOfDesign: Inspect the vendor qualification SOP, approved vendor list and COA reliance criteria.
testOfEffectiveness: For sampled component lots confirm supplier was approved, identity testing performed, and periodic full testing done where COAs are relied on.
checklist: Was the supplier approved before use?
Is identity testing performed on every lot?
controls.recommendation: Qualify suppliers before use and periodically verify COA reliability by full testing.

controls.title: Complaints are investigated by the quality unit
controls.objective: Product complaints are logged, assessed and investigated with CAPA where needed.
testOfDesign: Inspect the complaint handling SOP for timelines, QU review and trending.
testOfEffectiveness: For sampled complaints confirm QU review, investigation where warranted and closure within timelines.
checklist: Is every complaint reviewed by QU?
Are complaints trended?
controls.recommendation: Ensure QU review of all complaints and trend them by product and defect type.

controls.title: GMP self-inspection programme is planned and followed up
controls.objective: Self-inspections cover all GMP areas on a risk basis and observations are closed.
controls.risk: GMP gaps undetected until regulatory inspection.
testOfDesign: Inspect the self-inspection plan for coverage, frequency and auditor independence.
testOfEffectiveness: Confirm planned self-inspections were completed and observations closed with CAPA.
checklist: Did the plan cover all GMP areas?
Are observations closed?
controls.recommendation: Complete the risk-based self-inspection plan and track observations through CAPA to closure.
